method_observation.observation: Bunker-fuel recall stays high-yield when the probe follows one transaction from storage and credit through physical delivery, measurement, sampling, onboard handling and dispute resolution. It degrades quickly when it becomes a port-by-port supplier list or a current alternative-fuel readiness ranking. Future institutional probes should prefer transaction-chain failure points over actor enumeration.

proposed_validation_probe.reason: P005 closes the bunker-fuel transaction chain with high novelty. The compact atlas still reduces end-of-life supply adjustment largely to scrapping optionality, while the institutional chain from sale-for-recycling through cash buyers/intermediaries, demolition-yard capacity, scrap economics, hazardous-material and worker/environment constraints remains structurally important and orthogonal to the previous five passes.

stop_reason: The preset questions were answered with a coherent bunker transaction and infrastructure topology. Marginal recall then shifted toward exact supplier lineages, port licensing dates, standard thresholds, current hub rankings and legal outcomes; those require claim-scoped Evidence or would violate the sparse-map anti-tunnel rule.
